features.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Bye-mageddon means getting comfortable with the uncomfortable
features.desc: A bye-laden Week 11 might make you cringe at some of your lineup decisions, so let the facts hone your feelings on Bo Nix, Tony Pollard, Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave, Malik Nabers, Stefon Diggs and Colston Loveland.
body: Employing the crying laughing emoji (officially named Face with Tears of Joy) with unabashed enthusiasm.
Telling a perfect stranger you like their shoes.
Gasping with delight at the sight of livestock roaming near the roadside.

A verb that once described the action of drawing back or recoiling in fear, disgust or pain has since morphed into a standalone adjective (or noun) used to describe anything that causes secondhand embarrassment or comes across as awkward.

But to whom? Who exactly is so deeply troubled by these random acts of mirth? Maybe I've been too busy sorting aDOT and YAC (yikes) to notice, but has a single person or, perhaps, a coalition of judges been appointed as the Official Arbiters of Taste?
Given how much "cringe" is referenced, I imagine there must exist a chronically online task force set up to systematically stamp out any whimsy, frivolity and/or earnestness.
After all, the only thing worse than being a try-hard is to actually try hard at something.

I don't clap when the plane lands. But two months ago, I sat next to a young woman who did her best "When Harry Met Sally" impression and let out a boisterous, "OH, THANK GOD!" the second we touched down at O'Hare.

My dated movie reference aside, her outburst genuinely amused me. Was it cringe? Sure. Still, I bet the flight crew was deeply touched when she personally thanked every single one of them for helping her overcome a crippling fear of flying.
Have we become so afraid of looking foolish that we've stopped expressing delight... or worse, stopped feeling it altogether?

features.headline: Tarik Skubal free agency tracker: Latest on top MLB free agent
features.desc: Who will land the two-time Cy Young Award winner? We have all the latest updates on where things stand.
body: All eyes are on ace Tarik Skubal as MLB free agency gets underway ahead of the impending labor stoppage.

The current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, meaning that after that, no players can sign until a new CBA is established. This could put Skubal on the fast track to a new contract, as many around the sport expect him to sign ahead of the lockout.
Where do things currently stand in Skubal's free agency? What's the latest? We have everything you need to know about the winter's No. 1 free agent in one place.
Skubal met with the New York Mets on Monday and the Los Angeles Dodgers and Toronto Blue Jays on Tuesday. He is expected to round out his in-person get-togethers with the San Diego Padres this week.
By the time he signs — and it could be sooner than later — it will be the largest deal for a pitcher in baseball history. Read more in Jeff Passan's MLB free agency preview

features.headline: Why Packers can't protect Jordan Love or rush successfully
features.desc: The two-year demise of the Packers' offensive line began on March 10, 2025, and has no end in sight.
body: GREEN BAY, Wis. — The beginning of the downfall of the Green Bay Packers' offensive line can be traced to a specific day: March 10, 2025.
That was when general manager Brian Gutekunst signed then-San Francisco 49ers guard Aaron Banks to a four-year, $77 million free agent deal.

Not only have the Packers not gotten their money's worth out of Banks due to injuries and poor performance, but his signing set in a motion a game of musical chairs at just about every position on the line.

The result was what the Packers put on display in their most recent showing, the obliteration of their pass protection by the Minnesota Vikings in Sunday's 30-10 loss at Lambeau Field. In between that March 2025 day and Sunday has been 20 months of trying to get the offensive line settled.

Combine that with a position coach, Luke Butkus, and an offensive coordinator, Adam Stenavich, who have come under fire, and there's plenty of blame to go around for nearly two seasons' worth of offensive line issues.
"I think it's easy to pinpoint and point the finger and everybody wants to pinpoint blame, but the blame can go to everybody," coach Matt LaFleur said this week. "It's all of us in this together.
Certainly it starts with myself and then it goes to everybody else. It's coaches and players collectively."

He started all this by signing Banks, who had played all but six of his 2,464 snaps for the 49ers at left guard. The problem was the Packers already had a left guard. A two-time Pro Bowl left guard in Elgton Jenkins.

features.headline: 2027 NFL draft: Dolphins, Titans, Eagles, Jets, Chargers in race for No. 1 pick
features.desc: Five NFL teams have at least 5% odds to land the No. 1 pick in 2027, per ESPN's Football Power Index: the Dolphins, Titans, Eagles, Jets and Chargers.
features.by: NFL Nation, Jordan Reid and Seth Walder
body: The race for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL draft is taking shape now that we're 10 weeks into the 2026 season.

Five teams have at least a 5% chance at landing the top pick, according to ESPN's Football Power Index projections. So we called on our experts and reporters to size up each of those bottom-tier franchises at midseason.

NFL analyst Seth Walder used the FPI to make sense of each of the five teams' schedules the rest of the way. Our NFL Nation reporters looked at the biggest positional needs that could be addressed in the first round in April.
And NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid spun it forward and suggested one prospect each front office could consider if it landed that top selection.
Let's start with the Dolphins, who currently have the best odds at the No. 1 pick.
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 41.2% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 93%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
Not only are the Dolphins not favored by the FPI in a single remaining game this season, but the model also makes them at least a field-goal underdog in every game.

Their best chances to win are versus the Jets in Week 12, versus the Chargers in Week 16 and at the Patriots in Week 18. But because the FPI believes the Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL, they are not likely to win any of those contests.
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
The Dolphins have needs across the board, but if we're narrowing down positions that make sense at their projected draft slot, it's edge rusher, quarterback and wide receiver.

features.headline: Giannis changed everything, including Miami's margin for error
features.desc: The Heat landed their superstar, but it's the rest of their roster that could define their season.
body: AFTER WATCHING THE Los Angeles Lakers hand his team a 21-point loss, Miami Heat coach Erik Spoelstra opted to watch his mouth.
"I'm trying not to go on a rant right now," Spoelstra said following the Nov. 2 road setback that dropped Miami to 2-5.
The defeat proved to be rock bottom for the Heat, and the lack of trust and effort on the defensive end dominated the discussion in the visitors' locker room.

The offense also left a lot to be desired, especially the fit between blockbuster trade acquisition Giannis Antetokounmpo and Miami mainstay Bam Adebayo, who had scored in single digits twice during the Heat's season-opening four-game losing streak.

Still, the Heat maintained that this wasn't trending toward a lost season, even as their record was barely better than that of the Milwaukee Bucks team that Antetokounmpo had just left after 13 years.

"Do I think we have the pieces? Yeah," Antetokounmpo said. "Do I think we've got a lot of things to figure out? We have a lot, but I know what the Miami Heat culture is about. I know what the players in this locker room are about. I know what I'm about.
"I know that once we get on the right track, we can make some noise."
After stumbling out of the gates, the Heat have given ammunition to support Antetokounmpo's assertion, winning six of seven games since the lopsided loss to the Lakers.

The first three of those were against the league's cellar dwellers, but they've since added double-digit victories over playoff-tested teams such as the Cleveland Cavaliers, Detroit Pistons and Houston Rockets.

features.headline: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's top moments at Arrowhead Stadium
features.desc: Kelce's greatest Arrowhead moments include his first catch, lots of playoff magic, and meeting the love of his life, Taylor Swift.
body: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — Travis Kelce gets goosebumps every time, even though the drive from his home to his place of employment, at this point in his 14-year career, is routine.
On game days, his car enters Gate 5, the road that leads to the entrance of the Kansas City Chiefs' training facility. The destination of his journey always makes Kelce smile.
"You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere," Kelce said recently. "That's the best feeling for me."
Few players in the Chiefs' 67-year history have entered Arrowhead to put on the team's red jersey, helmet and cleats as many times as Kelce.

On Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Kelce will become only the fourth player in franchise history — joining Hall of Fame right guard Will Shields, kicker Nick Lowery and punter Dustin Colquitt — to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, a venue that opened in 1972.
Kelce considers Arrowhead a revered place, even before the venue was the site where his relationship with Taylor Swift, his wife, became public.

Whenever Kelce's illustrious career ends — which could happen after this season — he will be remembered for being one of the franchise's greatest players and at minimum a three-time Super Bowl champion.
He is also proud that his play, and most of his memorable highlights, will be synonymous with the history of Arrowhead, which is expected to have its final season in 2030.

"The fans love to fill that stadium and create those memories and get away from the realities of what the world is," Kelce said. "I just love the fact that they pour so much into it. It just makes you want to play that much harder for them. That definitely makes Arrowhead special."
